summary: The note surveys ten technology trends that Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs) can use to advance social entrepreneurship, including AI, blockchain, mobile, IoT, VR/AR, big data, social media, e-commerce, collaboration tools and 3D printing. Each trend is illustrated with an example enterprise and its launch timing between 2023 and 2024. It concludes that aligning with these trends supports both economic success and a more equitable, sustainable future, with profit and purpose as dual objectives.
one_line: Ten technology trends, each with an example company, show how SMEs can advance social entrepreneurship and combine profit with purpose.
key_facts: Social entrepreneurship is the practice of leveraging business to address social problems.
Sarah Johnson, founder of TechForGood Inc., says that since integrating AI in late September 2023 the company has personalized learning materials for over 10,000 students in underserved communities.
On October 15, 2023, GreenChain, a mid-sized ethical-sourcing clothing enterprise, adopted blockchain to track the provenance of its raw materials.
In November 2023, Mark Thompson, CEO of HealthMobilizer, showed how his SME used smartphones to give remote communities access to medical consultations and interventions.

Catherine Li's company SustainaTech launched an IoT solution in December 2023 that uses soil-moisture sensors to trigger irrigation only when necessary, helping small-scale farmers conserve water and cut costs.
EduRealms started using VR for vocational training in early 2024, simulating real-world scenarios for trades such as plumbing and electrical work.
Community Insight, a small consulting firm for nonprofits, has used big data analytics since June 2024 to pinpoint community needs with unprecedented precision.
On September 5, 2023, the platform ImpactCircle helped raise significant funds for disaster relief in record time.
EarthWear, a fashion brand founded by Jessica Lee, launched its online store in late September 2023 and significantly expanded its customer base while promoting sustainability.
In early 2024, ConnectForChange implemented a suite of collaborative tools that let it partner seamlessly with international NGOs.
ReBuild, an SME specializing in affordable housing, began using 3D printing to create cost-effective and environmentally friendly building materials.
The note concludes that staying informed and adaptable is key for SMEs to align their business models with the dual objectives of profit and purpose.
